text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- More than 120 million Indonesians are expected to go to polls today with a last reminder from President Suharto that their vote will count towards orderly and peaceful change.

- Thailand will lodge a protest with Kuala Lumpur over use of two cartoons in a Malaysian newspaper which portrayed Thailand as a prostitute haven and stricken with Aids, a Thai Foreign Ministry spokesman says.
- Malaysian Foreign Minister Datuk Abdullah Ahmad Badawi says he has not received any protest from the Thai government over the cartoons.
- Nine teenage schoolboys were among 12 youths arrested for breaking into a school's Singnet account and surfing Internet for free over six-month period.
- Historic Fullerton Square, which failed to secure a buyer last year, up for sale again in revamped offer which could save developer more than Singapore $30 million in costs.

- DBS Land has no immediate plans to buy more Parkway Holdings shares -- but it does not rule out doing so if "there are more shares available at the correct price", says deputy chairman and group chief executive officer Han Cheng Fong.
- Thai Cabinet approves Finance Ministry proposal to cut banking taxes to boost offshore banking activities and make Bangkok regional financial hub.
- Amid signs high-end disk drive market may be softening, market leader Seagate Technology said to have cut high-end production in Singapore.
- Trendy Hongkong clothing retailer Theme International, which is selling 20 percent stake to China Everbright group, may soon end up owning Singapore's Emporium Holdings.
- Fewer Singaporeans patronising Genting casino in Malaysia in the wake of row between the two countries, Genting Bhd officials say.
- Malaysia's Public Bank plans to let foreigners buy its local shares in a proposal that would interest many other companies here and across Causeway which also have foreign ownership limits.
- Funai Electric Co of Japan suing judicial managers of financially troubled Amcol Holdings, now being taken over by Indonesia's Sinar Mas Group.
- United Engineers (M) Bhd may defer listing of its wholly-owned toll operator Plus for a couple of months if poor sentiment continues.
- Bankers swarmed to finance Hongkong Land Holdings when it went to capital market for HK$3.6 billion loan, leading the property arm of Jardine Matheson Holdings to raise loan amount to HK$6 billion.
- Transpac Industrial Holdings will increase its investments in Taiwanese cable TV operator United Multi Media by subscribing to new shares to be issued.
